questions.q: You did not hear the teacher. What do you say?
questions.e: This politely asks someone to say it again.

questions.q: You want to borrow a classmate's ruler. What do you ask?
questions.e: “Could I borrow…” is a polite request.

questions.q: A friend says they passed an exam. What do you say?
questions.e: Use “Congratulations” to celebrate success.

questions.q: You are not sure about the answer. What do you say?
questions.e: “I'm not certain” shows doubt politely.

questions.q: You want to know the price in a shop. What do you ask?
questions.e: Ask “How much does it cost?” about a price.

questions.q: Your friend offers you tea, but you do not want any. What do you say?
questions.e: “No, thank you” refuses politely.

questions.q: You arrive at a meeting late. What do you say?
questions.e: Apologize with “I'm sorry I'm late.”

questions.q: You want to suggest studying together. What do you say?
questions.e: “Shall we…?” makes a suggestion.

questions.q: You want to check that a friend is okay. What do you ask?
questions.e: “Are you all right?” asks about someone's well-being.

questions.q: You did not understand the directions. What do you say?
o: Could you explain the way again?
questions.e: Ask the person to explain again.

questions.q: A classmate thanks you for helping. What do you reply?
questions.e: “You're welcome” is a common reply to thanks.

questions.q: You need a little more time to finish. What do you ask?
o: Could you give me a moment?
questions.e: “Give me a moment” asks for a short delay.

questions.q: You want to make sure someone received your message. What do you ask?
questions.e: This checks whether the message arrived.

questions.q: You agree with your classmate's idea. What do you say?
questions.e: Use “I think so too” to agree.

questions.q: You want to leave a phone call politely. What do you say?
o: I have to go now. Speak to you later.
questions.e: This politely ends a call.

questions.q: A friend asks for your opinion. What can you say?
o: At my opinion, it is useful.
For my opinion, it is useful.
In my opinion, it is useful.
questions.e: “In my opinion” introduces a view.

questions.q: You want a person to wait briefly. What do you say?
questions.e: This is a polite request to wait.

questions.q: You want to ask whether a seat is free. What do you ask?
questions.e: “Is this seat taken?” asks if it is occupied.

questions.q: You forgot someone's name. What do you say?
o: I'm sorry, could you remind me of your name?
questions.e: This politely asks the person to say their name again.

questions.q: You want to praise a friend's drawing. What do you say?
questions.e: “You did a great job” gives praise.

questions.q: You want to know when the bus leaves. What do you ask?
o: What time does the bus leave?
How much is the bus leave?
How often did the bus left?
questions.e: Ask “What time…” for a departure time.

questions.q: Your friend is worried before a test. What do you say?
o: You'll do your best. Good luck!
questions.e: This encourages the friend and wishes success.

questions.q: You want to invite a neighbour for lunch. What do you say?
o: Would you like to have lunch with us?
questions.e: “Would you like…” makes a polite invitation.

questions.q: You want to clarify a time. What do you ask?
o: Do you mean at half past two?
questions.e: This checks that you understood the time correctly.
